title: Throughput Sleuth — Field Report (Bisect & Canary)
summary: This is a compact field report from an on-call driven investigation into a 15% sustained throughput drop observed in the us-west cluster between 2025-07-13T22:00 and 2025-07-14T02:00. The investigation combined dashboard signal triage, targeted load replays, and a controlled canary/bisect of recent runtime commits and configuration flips. Key finding: a change in the batching heuristic combined with a new kernel launch path produced pathological small-batch behavior under the observed request size distribution.
timeline:
2025-07-13 22:05 - Alert fires: throughput drop (p50 token/sec) on prod-us-west serving group.
2025-07-13 22:10 - Pager ack; initial dashboard review.
2025-07-13 22:25 - Identified correlated CPU steal and increased tail latency for small requests.
2025-07-13 22:40 - Spawned local load generator to reproduce in staging; reproduced with synthetic mix matching client headers.
2025-07-13 23:15 - Bisect candidate set prepared (commits from last 72h + config flips).
2025-07-14 00:30 - Canaryed individual commits; isolate commit c3f9a2a as first-regression candidate.
2025-07-14 01:45 - Rollback of batching heuristic change applied to a canary pool; throughput recovers.
2025-07-14 02:00 - Short postmortem notes and mitigation plan drafted.
reproduction:
Load profile used: mix of tokens-per-request {short:60%, medium:30%, long:10%} with request inter-arrival matching observed 95th percentile burstiness.
Command (loadgen): ./tools/loadgen --target prod-us-west-canary --qps 4200 --mix short:0.6,medium:0.3,long:0.1 --seed 20250713 --concurrency 120
Staging reproduction notes: reproduces on rtx-a100 pools when batching threshold is set to <= 12 tokens/req; does not reproduce when batching threshold >= 32. Also reproduces under tiny batch kernels on Ampere nodes but not on older kernels.
Artifacts: trimmed request corpus saved as s3://redwood-inc/perf/repro-corpora/2025-07-13-small-batch.tar.gz
diagnostics:
Quick signals that helped narrow scope:
- CPU steal spikes localized to worker processes that handled short requests.
- KV cache hit-rate unchanged; points away from cache regression.
- p99 latency correlated with drop in average batch size (prom metric batch_size_avg).
- Perf maps and cpu flamegraphs sampled via py-spy show disproportionate time in kernel-launch shim for batches < 16.
Useful commands and outputs (summary):
- pprof (go service): go tool pprof -http=:8080 ./bin/service cpu.prof -> showed hotspots in kernel_selector.go:allocateKernelForBatch
- strace spot-check on one worker: observed repeated clone/open syscalls for small batches; suggests new path opened temporary IPC handles.
- BPF trace: tcp_retransmits and socket-accept patterns normal; rules out network degradation.
- gpu profiler: nvprof traces show kernel invocation overhead dominates for <16 tokens.
Attached mini-samples: flame_short.svg, flame_medium.svg (linked in artifacts).
metric_queries:
PromQL snippets used in dashboards and ad-hoc checks:
- avg by(pool) (irate(serving_tokens_processed_total[1m])) -> throughput per pool
- histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(serving_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool)) -> p99 latency by pool
- sum(rate(serving_batches_created_total[1m])) by (pool, batch_size) -> batch creation rate by size
- rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job="worker"}[1m]) / count(node_cpu_seconds_total) -> rough per-worker CPU pressure
- sum(rate(kernel_launchs_total[1m])) by (kernel_impl) -> expose which kernel path invoked
Notes: dashboard annotations aligned with bisect steps to visualize when commits/config flips were applied.
bisect_steps:
Strategy: binary bisect over three dimensions (code commits, config flips, kernel variants).
1) Build candidate set: commits in last 72h + config flags toggled in same period (N~18).
2) Create paired canaries (A=baseline, B=test) with identical infra.
3) Apply loadgen reproduction for 30m to each, collect batch_size_avg, throughput, p99.
4) If B regresses, split candidate set and continue.
Result: isolated to commit c3f9a2a which introduced 'adaptive_batch_small_path=true' with a rewritten kernel selector.
Notes: when we bisected only commits (keep configs constant), commit c3f9a2a still reproduced. When we reverted only the config flag on top of the commit, regression disappeared, so the commit+flag interaction triggered the path.
canary_comparison:
Canary diff approach used: side-by-side time-series + request-sample inspection. Key artifacts:
- Canary panel showing throughput, avg_batch_size, p99, kernel_path_ratio.
- Request sampling: 1% of requests traced and payloads hashed to compare serialization time.
Findings: canary B (with change) shows 45% increase in kernel_launchs_total for batches <16 and 12% lower avg_batch_size. Sampled requests show identical payloads but increased per-request kernel handshake (~300-600us extra).
Decision: roll back config 'adaptive_batch_small_path' in prod-canary, monitor for 1 hour, then apply full rollback across pools if stable. Rolling back returned throughput to baseline within 10 minutes.
action_items:
1) Immediate: revert 'adaptive_batch_small_path' flag in prod and write temporary guard to prevent rollout until kernel warmup added (owner: Rana).
2) Short-term: add regression test in CI that runs small-batch microbench for any kernel selector changes (owner: Miguel).
3) Medium-term: instrument batch creation to emit batch_size_distribution with 5ms granularity and add alert when avg_batch_size drops by >10% relative to 1h baseline (owner: Aisha).
4) Follow-up: design a lightweight kernel warmup to avoid per-request handshake on first use (owner: eng-serving-runtime-ops).
5) Postmortem: schedule 1-hour blameless review to capture root cause write-up and update rollout gating (owner: product-hosted-api).
notes_to_followup:
Unresolved questions:
- Why did the kernel selector prefer the small-batch path for a subset of nodes? Hypothesis: stale capability flags at node bootstrap time. Need to audit bootstrap sequence.
- Check if any clients shifted request-size distribution prior to the drop; correlate with client releases (INF-8721).
Observations for future incidents:
- Small-batch kernel overheads can dominate on modern GPUs; always include microbench for <16 token cases in perf PRs.
- Canary panels should include a derived metric 'batch_headroom' = max_batch_size - avg_batch_size to catch approaching pathological regimes.
Link to raw artifacts: s3://redwood-inc/perf/artifacts/2025-07-14-throughput-sleuth/
